clue.text: Short broadcast including a siren prepared for preliminary event

parts.note: curt means brief or short in manner

indicators.note: something that includes another thing holds it within itself, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

indicators.note: to prepare something is to work it up into a new form, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A brief radio programme featuring a wailing siren is laid on as a warm-up event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short broadcast' looks like one phrase for a brief programme, but 'Short' and 'broadcast' each give their own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser is literally a short play staged before the main one, and by extension any opening or warm-up occasion.

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone fills up their vehicle and drives off.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods carried by a ship, plane or lorry, which is to say its load or freight.

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
prizes handed over at a ceremony are presentations

explanation.surface: People grumbling about who received the prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaints about awards' reads as one phrase, but 'Complaints' alone is the definition and 'about' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make representations is to lodge formal protests or objections, so the plural noun works as grievances voiced to an authority.

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An organiser who runs a gala poorly ends up worn out and thin from the stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Angular describes a bony, lean figure with sharp corners showing, much as a haggard or skinny person looks.

clue.text: Interact with odd characters out to be smart

indicators.note: throwing out the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones in place

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: Advice to mix with strange people only to drop them in order to look stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' here means odd-numbered, not strange: removing letters one, three, five and seven leaves the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and smart are synonyms for being tidy, trim and well turned out in appearance.

clue.text: Incredible article on time put into measurement of water depth

indicators.note: one piece placed on top of another in a down clue comes before it

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: putting one thing into another sets it inside, so a piece is placed within a longer one

parts.note: a sounding is a measurement of how deep water is, taken with a line or sonar
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at how a clock was dropped into a depth reading of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the article comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounding means so surprising as to be scarcely believable, a close synonym of amazing or unbelievable.

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to race is to rush
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bartender hurries because a drink order is arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a classic mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Mad scandal mayor sorted out for prime minister

indicators.note: sorting things out puts them into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazy affair involving a mayor is dealt with by the head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsay MacDonald was Britain's first Labour prime minister, leading governments in 1924 and from 1929 to 1935.

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics

indicators.note: a wrecked thing is smashed apart, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
ancient means old

explanation.surface: Troops arriving smash up a historic building.
explanation.definitionFit: Freehold is outright ownership of land or buildings with no time limit, and by extension the property so owned.

clue.text: Payment to shelter dog not available? Disgusting

indicators.note: sheltering something means covering it on both sides, so the outer word wraps around the rest

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for a home
a pug is a small breed of dog
NA is the abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A landlord won't house a pet, which is sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the stretch from 'dog' to 'available', which reads as a pet being unavailable.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant and disgusting are synonyms for something that provokes strong distaste or revulsion.

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for strange or peculiar
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A strange newspaper editor supports a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum meaning odd is chiefly British and dated, as in 'a rum business'.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance, so as a verb it means to object or protest.

clue.text: Just occupied by exercises in public

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has it inside, so one piece fills the middle of another

parts.note: just and only both mean merely
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Someone's time is taken up with workouts done where everyone can see.
explanation.definitionFit: Openly means without concealment, in full view of others, which is what doing something in public amounts to.

indicators.note: a filling sits inside whatever it fills, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A shopper purchases tea and stuffs it into a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To purchase is to acquire something by paying for it, an exact synonym of the verb to buy.

clue.text: React to art reproduced in reddish-brown colour

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy made afresh, so these letters are put together again differently

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic responds to an artwork that has been copied in a rusty brown shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is unglazed brownish-red fired clay, and the name is used for that earthy orange-brown hue.

clue.text: Leader needing attention, in bad shape and beginning to despair

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here added at the end
placing one thing in another sets it within, so a piece is inserted
something in bad shape is out of order, so the word that follows is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to give someone your ear is to pay attention
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A leader in poor condition and starting to lose hope needs looking after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bad shape' looks like an idiom for unwell, but it splits into an insertion signal, an anagram signal and the word to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearhead is the person or group at the front of an attack or campaign, so it means the one who leads.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a judge declares the punishment for a convicted person
second meaning: a complete unit of words with a subject and verb

explanation.surface: A pedant criticises someone's syntax.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to impose a punishment in court; as a noun it is a complete grammatical unit of words.

clue.text: Part of poem originally about lover

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters read right to left
only part of the words is wanted, so a run of letters is lifted from inside them

parts.note: the run straddles the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A section of verse was first written about a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'poEM ORiginally' and must be read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo is the archetypal young suitor, so his name is used for any ardent male admirer.

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-image, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
on means forward, as in 'move on'

explanation.surface: Remarks offered once someone has thought things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put forward' looks like one phrase meaning proposed, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are brief written remarks or observations, as in notes on a text, so they serve as comments.

clue.text: Faces swimming large lake to reach mountain

indicators.note: things swimming about move freely, so the letters drift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Swimmers cross a big lake on the way to a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Scafell is a peak in the English Lake District, neighbour of Scafell Pike, England's highest mountain.

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: something holding another has it in its grasp, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
an ounce is an imperial unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone gave up their rightful goal while carrying a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right purpose' reads as a proper aim, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce is to give up formally, so renounced means abandoned, as with a claim or belief.

clue.text: Politician with anger restricted by American judges

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it on both sides

parts.note: US is short for American

indicators.note: with simply puts one piece alongside the next

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: An angry politician is held back by judges from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' looks like a verb in the surface but works as a plural noun for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpires are officials who rule on play in sports such as cricket and tennis, so they judge, either as noun or verb.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, stressed on the second syllable: to delight or bewitch
second meaning, stressed on the first syllable: the act of going in

explanation.surface: Someone uses charisma to get through the door.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently, en-TRANCE and EN-trance.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to captivate or delight; an entrance is the act of coming in, which is gaining admittance.

indicators.note: something happening during another falls within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A team falls silent while losing a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside S + ROUT, just after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprout is to begin growing, as seeds put out shoots, so the verb is a synonym of grow.

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lifted from within

parts.note: the run straddles three words

explanation.surface: Some people can't bear what a stew tastes like.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'deteST A STEw'; the 's acts as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste and flavour are synonyms for the sensation a food or drink produces in the mouth.

clue.text: Root initially under stone I move

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another is written after it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener says they shift a stone so as to get at a root below it.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is 14 pounds, used in Britain for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to move slightly or begin to move, as someone stirring in their sleep.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a noun: the end of something
second meaning, an adjective: very friendly

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are also pronounced differently, with a Z sound and an S sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of a day is its end; close friends share an affectionate, familiar bond.

clue.text: Tests to carry out, designed to provide lessons

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so a piece is placed within another

parts.note: trials are tests

indicators.note: a design is a fresh layout, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Trials are carried out that are intended to teach something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry out' reads as one phrase meaning perform, but 'carry' holds the next word inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorials are teaching sessions, often small-group classes with a tutor, so they are a kind of lesson.

indicators.note: things jumping about leap out of position, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete clears the principal obstacles in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie is the Booker-winning author of Midnight's Children and The Satanic Verses.
